record.clinical_notes: Patient presented with a 2-day history of periumbilical pain migrating to the right iliac fossa, associated with low-grade fever and vomiting. On examination, tenderness and guarding at McBurney's point with positive Rovsing's sign. USG abdomen showed a non-compressible, dilated appendix (9mm) with peri-appendiceal fat stranding, confirming acute appendicitis. Patient was taken up for emergency laparoscopic appendectomy under general anaesthesia. Intraoperatively, an inflamed, non-perforated appendix was noted; appendectomy performed uneventfully with no intraoperative complications. Post-op recovery was uneventful, patient tolerated oral feeds by day 2, ambulated independently, and was discharged in stable condition with advice for wound care and follow-up.
